main_text.p: Ex ijs quae jam nobis dicta sunt, the-sim colligimus: Cum Domini Dei nostri causa conditi simus & uiuamus,non esse cur serui taedio aut dolore fracti,uitae donum sibi aspernandum putent. Semper itaq; in conspectu nobis sit dictum Pauli: Nullus enim nostrûm sibijpsi uiuit,& nullus sibijpsi moritur. Nam siue uiuimus, Domino uiuimus: siue morimur, Domino morimur. Siue igitur uiuamus, siue moriamur, Domini sumus. Rom. 14. 7. 8.
main_text.head: VERSVS IIII.

p.i: Dixit autem Jehouah: Nonne uehemes ira est tibi? Aut, Nunquid benefacit tibi ira?

main_text.p: Hieronymus, Verbũ, ait, הֵיטֵב חָרָה לָךְ[?], & Iratus es tu, & Contristatus es tu, transferri potest, quod utrum q; & Prophetae & Domini personae conuenit: quòd uel iratus sit, ne uideretur apud Niniuitas esse men titus: uel contristatus, intelliges Israelem esse periturum.
Thesis: Deus merito irridet acres illos motus cordium nostrorum, quos impatientia & tristicia pariunt.

page.notes: The Hebrew phrase after "Verbũ, ait," is only partly legible; the reading given is a best guess (marked [?]). The "Aut," before "Nunquid" is preceded by a bracket-like sign that is not a letter and was left out. "Domini sumus" in the Rom. reference: the first letter of "sumus" is a long s and is read with some doubt. The "•" marks at line ends are ornaments, not text. "men titus" is printed with a space and is kept as printed.
